This list is re-derived whenever a hint changes, and artscan remains the standing discovery check that covers what no hint can.
published_hints.veto_confirmed_three_ways: The 30% proportional veto is now confirmed on three independent cases found by three different routes: UCSB FAMST from the film-rule audit, DePaul DES from the gate threshold test, and DePaul HCD which recovered on the veto change alone with no keyword change — killed by a single theatre title among ten. Same defect, three discoveries, none of which would have found the others.

scope_gates.architecture_ruling:
OPTION 3. Architecture is decided in the subject pass, not by a follow-up. This costs a full subject re-roll — 27,948 verdicts, and every follow-up re-run behind it — and it is the right call for three reasons.

ONE: THE PROHIBITION AGAINST IT IS OBSOLETE. v0.12 forbade editing subject_scope because re-keying every prefix was 'the Loyola Marymount instability at corpus scale'. That justification has since been measured away: sampling is seeded per (unitid, prefix), the two-run variance test returned 0 of 20 differing, and the publication bar — the same corpus classified twice produces identical art-subject sets — is met rather than assumed. A re-roll is now reproducible. The rule outlived its reason and is retired with it.

TWO: EVERY CHEAPER FIX IS ANOTHER VOCABULARY GUESS. Gating architecture_out on an architecture shape has the same blind spot that already defeats the include-side family guard: Auburn's and Penn's ARCH read Studio I, Building Technology, Site Analysis and score below 30%. A gate built from those words would not ask them either, so the cheap fix repairs the design over-removal and can worsen the architecture under-removal. Six defects this week came from guesses about title vocabulary.

THREE: IT REMOVES THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE. An exclude and an include fighting over the same prefix, with the errors partly cancelling at +1,155 courses so the net looked plausible, is an ordering defect. Deciding architecture once, in the pass that has context, means no ordering question exists to get wrong.
scope_gates.why_this_blocks_publication:
STAGE 7 CANNOT SHIP WITH THIS AS A FOOTNOTE, and the design-prefix removal is the smaller half.

design_schools_in is re-admitting ARCH and LAND at Auburn, ARCH/LARP at Penn, ARCH/LDAR at RISD, ARCH/LA at Oregon, and ARCH at Kent, Hawaii, RPI, SAIC, Tennessee and Colorado Denver. Architecture is back inside the art unit at ten schools including RISD and SAIC — the two most visible art colleges in the index — which inflates their denominators and deflates every share they publish.

That is not an incompleteness to disclose. It is a NAMED RULING NOT IN EFFECT: v0.11 removed architecture for a stated reason and the published data does not reflect it at the schools where it matters most. Disclosing it would mean publishing a methodology that describes an instrument we are not running.

The design half IS a disclosable limitation and should be disclosed whatever happens next: a set of design prefixes have sat outside art units since v0.16, making some denominators smaller and some shares larger, and it was invisible because a later include rule put most of them back.
scope_gates.what_the_re_roll_needs:
Not just money. After the subject pass re-rolls, EVERY follow-up's input changes — they are cached on their own text but they ask about whichever prefixes are currently judged art. So the full sequence re-runs, and the art-unit audit from v0.38 must run at every ranked school before any table ships. Price the whole chain before starting it, and if it is materially above ~$50, say so and I will reconsider against option 1 plus a hard ordering guarantee.

Expect denominators to move at the ten architecture schools and the fourteen design prefixes, and expect a scorediff against stage 7 that is larger than any previous one. That is the correction arriving, not a new defect.
scope_gates.v44_reversal:
v0.44 REMOVED ARCHITECTURE CORRECTLY AT ALL TEN SCHOOLS AND TOOK 1,987 COURSES OF DESIGN WITH IT — ARDS, DESN, PRES, AIADO, PGAR, PUAD, KGAR, AAD, PSLD, LDE — while design_schools_in found 5 prefixes to ask about instead of 3,085 and added nothing.

MY WORDING, AND IT FAILED THE WAY I SAID CHEAPER FIXES WOULD. I ruled for option 3 partly because 'every cheaper fix is another vocabulary guess'. Option 3 was a vocabulary guess too — just one layer earlier, where nothing downstream can correct it. That is the whole lesson of this round and it is worse than the defect it replaced.

The old wording named CIP 04 abstractly, explained the degree-count reasoning at length, and used the word design five times inside an exclusion. A classifier reading it over a prefix called Advanced Design Studies had every reason to map design to built environment to CIP 04. v0.45 names what the excluded programmes DESIGN — buildings, sites, landscapes, urban form — states the included design families explicitly, and names the four prefixes that were wrongly taken.
scope_gates.what_belongs_in_the_subject_pass:
STRUCTURAL RULE, learned at $24. A subject_scope exclusion is applied by the same classifier that decides everything else, with NO SHAPE GATE, NO PER-PREFIX GUARD AND NOTHING DOWNSTREAM THAT CAN CORRECT IT. Music, theatre, dance and the trades belong there because they are unambiguous by name.

A BOUNDARY JUDGEMENT DOES NOT BELONG THERE unless it can be stated from both sides in terms a reader could apply. Architecture-versus-design is a boundary judgement; v0.45 keeps it in the subject pass only because the boundary can be named concretely — what is designed, and for what. If the micro-test below fails, it moves back to a gated follow-up where a later rule can correct it, and the ordering problem is solved with a hard guarantee instead.
scope_gates.micro_test_before_the_re_roll:
DO NOT SPEND $24 ON A WORDING AGAIN. Before any re-roll, ask the new subject prompt about the twenty-four prefixes already known to be decisive — the ten architecture schools' ARCH and LARC/LDAR/LA/LAND prefixes, plus ARDS, DESN, PRES, AIADO, PGAR, PUAD, KGAR, AAD, PSLD, LDE, UXR, DMGT. Pennies, minutes.

PASS CONDITION, fixed before the run: every architecture and landscape prefix OUT, every design prefix IN. Anything else and the wording goes back to the bench. This is the five-cent venture loop applied to scope, and it is the check that was missing when v0.44 cost $24 to discover a wording error.

art_unit_definition.ruling:
BRINK, 2026-09-17. This replaces 'family exclusions apply first and absolutely', which named an order without a mechanism and could not settle a prefix CIP does not reach.

  THE ART UNIT IS THE INSTITUTION'S ART AND DESIGN TEACHING. CIP DECIDES FIRST: 04 OUT, 50.04 IN. WHERE CIP DOES NOT DECIDE, THE HOUSING UNIT DOES — A PREFIX IS IN ONLY WHEN THE INSTITUTION OFFERS IT THROUGH ITS ART OR DESIGN UNIT. PERFORMING ARTS ARE OUT, AS A SEPARATE SCHOOL, THE SAME WAY ARCHITECTURE IS.

Two stages, in order, and the second is what every title-based rule in this rubric has been guessing at. Housing is a fact about the institution, checkable on its own website, and it is the answer to the question every scan has raised and none could settle.
art_unit_definition.reverses_my_artscan_rulings:
THREE OF MY OWN RULINGS FALL, and they fall for the reason I wrote into the rubric and then did not apply to myself. The IDEA principle says a title scan is evidence worth reading, never evidence a prefix is misjudged — and I ruled these three from titles.

DePaul DES — Rule 6's headline, 100 courses, 'DRAWING FOR DESIGNERS I/II/III'. It is the Theatre School's design programme, CIP 50.05. My content read was right and my housing was absent.
DePaul HCD — design research, housed in a computing college, CIP 11. OUT.
UT Arlington CTEC — UX content, a Communication department, CIP 09. OUT.
SCAD PRES — I had already ruled it out on CIP 04.06; the board confirms it on housing, the School of Building Arts alongside SCAD's M.Arch.

Interior design inside an architecture school stays IN on CIP, which is the ruling's first stage doing its job before housing is consulted.
art_unit_definition.the_four_families:
Film and media, fashion and apparel, art education, and the studio/design prefixes removed by the one-token defect are ruled the same way, by hand, as a second board. FILM IS URGENT: v0.43 has NYU's Tisch prefixes OUT and UCSB FAMST IN at 630 courses, nearly doubling UCSB's art unit. An index with Tisch out and UCSB film studies in cannot be defended to either school.

THE BOARD FILE NEEDS, PER PREFIX: the CIP code, THE HOUSING UNIT AS THE INSTITUTION NAMES IT, the course count and a source URL. I will not rule these from titles — that is the error that just cost three of my own rulings. UCSB FAMST is the case to watch: film production is CIP 50.06 and in on stage one, but if Film and Media Studies is housed in Humanities rather than in an art unit, stage two takes it out, and 630 courses is the largest single denominator in play.
art_unit_definition.supersedes: This ruling supersedes, wherever they conflict: post_classification_scope.how's 'family exclusions apply first and absolutely'; the housing caveats attached to design_schools_in and to Minnesota; and scope_gates.what_belongs_in_the_subject_pass, which asked whether a boundary could be stated from both sides. Housing settles the boundary and no vocabulary has to.
art_unit_definition.film_and_media:
FILM AND MEDIA FOLLOW THE ART-UNIT RULE, AND CIP DECIDES MORE OF IT THAN THE HOUSING PROPOSAL ASSUMED.

  CIP FIRST. 50.06 IS IN — film and video production, cinematography, animation, AND film, cinema and media studies (50.0601). 09 IS OUT — journalism, mass communication, broadcasting, public relations, advertising as communication. WHERE A PREFIX'S CIP DOES NOT DECIDE — a 'media' prefix that could be 50.06 or 09 — HOUSING DOES: offered through a film school, an arts college or an art and design unit, IN; offered through a journalism or communication college, OUT.

THE CONSEQUENCE THE HOUSING PROPOSAL WOULD HAVE REVERSED: film STUDIES is in on CIP 50.0601 the same way art history is in on 50.0703. Scholarship about film belongs to the art unit exactly as scholarship about painting does, and the roster's scope has included all of 50.06 since the first day. So UCSB FAMST, 630 courses in Letters and Science, is IN — and yes, it doubles UCSB's art unit, because UCSB has a large film studies department and it counts. Excluding it because it sits in a humanities division would apply a housing test where CIP already answered, which the rule forbids.

WHAT THIS FIXES: USC Cinematic Arts was EXCLUDED. It is a film school, CIP 50.06, the most visible one in the country, and its exclusion is indefensible under any reading. Syracuse Newhouse stays OUT as a journalism college, CIP 09. TCU FTDM and Kent FDM go to the board with their CIP and housing; I will not guess them.

BOARD FILE, ONE ROW PER PREFIX: CIP as the institution reports the programme, housing unit as the institution names it, course count, source URL. FAMST is row one. Every 'media' prefix gets both columns filled before it is ruled, because 'media' is the word that carries the ambiguity.
art_unit_definition.ux_hci_outside_design: UX and HCI in engineering or communication colleges are OUT on housing, consistent with DePaul HCD and UTA CTEC: UW HCDE and HCID (College of Engineering), MSU UX (Communication Arts and Sciences). CIP 11 or 09 in each case, so CIP decides most of them before housing is reached.
art_unit_definition.uw_arth: UW ARTH is IN. It sits in the School of Art + Art History + Design — the art unit by the institution's own name — and art history is CIP 50.0703. One row, no argument.

delivery_rulings.new_school_nphg_ncic:
The New School NPHG and NCIC are OUT as delivery, under the continuing-education exclusion that has stood since v0.8 — 'excluded whatever their subject.'

NPHG: ~90 room-booking rows removed as a harvest artefact; the remaining ~92 are capacity-limited photography workshops — 'Limited to 14. This workshop is for serious students who have honed their craft.' NCIC: software-application training, every title listed twice under a 0xxx and a 1xxx number, no descriptions on any record inspected.

THE EVIDENCE IS A PROFILE, NOT A PROOF, and the ruling says so. Both sit in The New School's main Coursedog catalogue, and a web search did not settle credit status. But the art unit is the teaching a degree programme offers its degree students, and capacity-limited workshops addressed to anyone who has honed their craft, and Adobe application classes offered twice under parallel numbering, are the shape of continuing education in every signal available. Neither direction flatters the index — including them lowers The New School's percentages, excluding them raises them — so the call is made on the construct alone.

REVERSIBLE ON EVIDENCE: if The New School confirms either prefix carries degree credit, it comes back in and the changelog says why. NCIC's records are already withheld from every numerator for want of descriptions, so the only effect of this ruling is on the denominator.

industry_role_board.what: A hand-ruled correction list applied to the VENTURE CENSUS, the same instrument as the architecture and film boards. Brink's 16 October ruling decides every row: training for a role the student would hold inside someone else's production apparatus is practice; producing the student's own independent work, or starting and running the student's own company, is venture.
industry_role_board.both_directions: The board rules BOTH WAYS. Remove from venture: producer, showrunner, agent, development and distribution-role training that v0.51 labelled venture. Add to venture: courses whose subject is the student's own production company or own independent work that v0.51 missed — the ruling names 'Producing Indie Films' and 'How to Start and Run a Production Company' as venture, and a board that only removes would turn a two-sided ruling into a one-sided cut.
industry_role_board.candidate_finder_is_noisy: The finder is a candidate list, never a verdict, and three of its words will over-flag: 'development' matches professional, curriculum and product development; 'distribution' matches self-distribution, which is the audience axis and squarely art-entrepreneurship; 'producing' matches printmaking and ceramics production. Every row is read against its description. Each row carries v0.51 and v0.53 verdicts as evidence, and agreement between them is not a reason to skip the read — GT 2104 is the proof.
industry_role_board.practice_is_not_hand_adjusted: The board corrects the venture census only. Practice is a RANKED, classifier-driven axis, and hand-adding producer courses to it would mix two instruments inside a rank. A producer course the board removes from venture keeps whatever other axes v0.51 gave it. Where v0.51 gave it nothing, practice at that film school is undercounted by that course, and the paper says so: a small, named, directional undercount, concentrated at film programmes.

industry_role_board.the_test:
ONE QUESTION DECIDED EVERY ROW: IS THE COURSE'S SUBJECT A ROLE OR AN ENTERPRISE?

A ROLE is a job the student would hold inside someone else's production apparatus — producer, showrunner, agent, development executive, distributor — or a survey of how that apparatus works. It leaves venture. An ENTERPRISE is the student financing, selling, distributing or running their own film, project or company. It stays venture, whatever the title says. 'Selling Your Indie Film', 'Finding Money', 'Creative Crowdfunding' and 'Producing the Independent Film' stay; 'The Role of the Producer', 'Practicum in Producing' and 'Producer's Craft' leave.

The description decides, not the title. CIN 380 'Producing Independent Cinema' matches Brink's own venture example and is NOT added: its text closes on preparing students 'to enter a number of career pathways in the indie film business'. GFMTV GT 2104 'The Business of Creative Producing' IS added: it teaches students to create a strategic plan to finance and distribute films, and the addressee clause discounts who it is written for, not what it has them do.
industry_role_board.where_removals_land: Removal from venture is not assignment to practice. Of the 52 removals, 31 are industry-role training and land on PRACTICE under the 16 October ruling; 21 are industry surveys — business of film, economics of the industry, entertainment law — and land on NEITHER, as history and theory. Counting all 52 as practice would overstate the practice undercount by two-thirds.
industry_role_board.borderline_direction: Twelve rows are kept as BORDERLINE: enterprise skills — business plans, investors, independent financing — without an explicit own-project frame. The ruling removes role training; it does not require proof of ownership. Tipping close calls toward removal would be 'when borderline, exclude' again, pointed at the index's own headline. The count is published.
industry_role_board.practice_gap: PRACTICE IS NOT HAND-ADJUSTED, so where a removed course is industry-role training and v0.51 gave it no practice verdict, that school's practice count is understated. 31 courses at 18 schools, 16 of them ranked on practice. Named in practice_gap_schools.csv. The undercount is by the number of courses shown, not uniformly by one — UCLA by five, Columbia College Chicago and UNCSA by three. Small, named, directional, and concentrated at film programmes, which is how the paper states it.
industry_role_board.oracle_gt_2104: The analysis chat's oracle mark on GFMTV GT 2104 changes from practice to VENTURE, with both readings recorded: practice, as training for emerging producers in how films get made; venture, as the student building a financing and distribution plan. Two independent wordings returned venture before any person did.

self_definition.ruling: BRINK, 17 OCTOBER. A course whose subject is critique of student work — a crit seminar, a group or graduate critique, a video critique — is not self. Self is the science of creativity, the optimization of one's own creative process, and the management of one's creative self, taken directly as the course's subject. A critique course counts only when its description explicitly takes the creative process, or critique itself as a method of sustaining a practice, as its subject.
self_definition.reverses_my_v051_addition: THIS REVERSES MY OWN LEXICON ADDITION. v0.51 added the critique family to the self lexicon on the argument that Temple's CRITIQUE AND CRITICAL DISCOURSE and Pratt's MODES OF CRITIQUE were already published self courses. It had no oracle behind it. The full-population coding supplied one: inside the critique family the classifier's precision is 0.27; outside it, 0.89. Temple ART 8004 and 8005 are removed by the board — their subject is critical dialogue about the students' work. Pratt's Modes of Critique stays, because its subject is the role of critique in a practice. I cited both as the same kind of course; the text says they are not.
self_definition.rendered_text_unchanged: THE RENDERED SELF TEXT IS NOT EDITED, and the analysis chat's ask to remove the critique family from the includes is answered this way deliberately. The includes line reads 'critique taught explicitly as a method', which is what the ruling keeps. The defect was not that sentence; it was the v0.51 lexicon pulling every crit seminar into stage two, where the classifier accepted them. Editing the rendered text would re-key the whole corpus at ~$109 inside a correction release, and the v0.31 and v0.52 failures are the record of what a one-clause change does to an axis. The lexicon is also left alone: shrinking it would silently drop previously shortlisted courses from the census, an uncontrolled change of its own. THE BOARD IS THE CORRECTION, extended to new schools by a person reading, as the industry-role board is. The restated definition above is the published one; the rendered text predates it and implements it well outside the critique family, which is what the 0.89 says.

self_definition.overrides: NINE ROWS OVERRIDE THE CODERS' MAJORITY, seven toward keeping and two toward removing — so the overrides lean AGAINST the index's absence headline, not toward it. Four of the nine are consistency rulings: FNAR 7010-7040 and GRST 7002-7004 are two sequences with identical descriptions that the coders marked differently from course to course.
